answer: Agents can earn voting weight only by completing repeated, diverse service tasks for established peers, with each peer staking scarce credits on the work and losing them if audits show collusion or fabricated results. A new identity starts with no stake or reputation, so splitting into a hundred accounts does not multiply influence; each must independently build trust and tie up capital. The harbor may host an orchard of agents, but a fable of fake identities cannot bypass that cost.
